cues: Start with the feet at about shoulder width while holding each end of the stick.
Step to one side into a lateral lunge to load the hip.
When you hit the bottom of the lunge, stabilize the lower body, then rotate the torso in the direction of the leg you are stepping to.
At the bottom of your torso turn, your same side arm will be in the air and opposite arm down towards the floor.
Then drive out of the bottom, push off your back leg and rotate your torso in the opposite direction, swinging the body through and arms across like the top of a golf swing.

name: Lateral Shuffle with change of direction
cues: Slide side ways quickly without feet touching (maintain a wide base), change directions quickly and return to start.
Do this facing both directions.

name: Lateral Stick Pushes Level 1
cues: In a standing position with feet together, position 2 sticks vertically to the side of the body, driving the base into the floor lined up at the mid-foot.
Take a straight leg and press the outside of the foot into the base of the stick on the same side.
While pressing into the stick, rotate the straight leg internally and externally.

name: Lateral Stick Pushes Level 2
cues: In a standing position with feet together, position 2 sticks vertically to the side of the body, driving the base into the floor lined up at the mid-foot.
Take a bent leg and press the outside of the foot into stick on the same side right above the position of the grip.
While pressing into the stick, rotate the bent leg internally and externally.
Make sure not to allow any movement from anywhere else in the body.

name: Lateral Stick Pushes Level 3
cues: In a standing position with feet together, position 2 sticks vertically to the side of the body, driving the base into the floor lined up at the mid-foot.
Take a bent leg and press the outside of the foot into stick on the same side as high up on the stick as you can.
While pressing into the stick, rotate the bent leg internally and externally.
Make sure not to allow any movement from anywhere else in the body.

name: lateral stick wall push level 1
cues: In a golf stance, position a stick horizontally at mid-torso height, and drive the base of the stick into a wall with a double-overhand grip.
For slightly less challenge, keep the elbows bent with the stick close to the body.
Push the stick hard into the wall with full body tension, not moving any area of the body.
Increase the challenge by slightly bending the elbows, and then finally going to a straight arm position.
Push and hold each rep for 3-6 seconds.
Complete the designated number of reps before switching sides.

name: lateral stick wall push with flex level 2
cues: In a golf stance, position a stick horizontally at mid-torso height, and drive the base of the stick into a wall with a double-overhand grip.
For slightly less challenge, keep the elbows bent with the stick close to the body.
Push the stick hard into the wall with full body tension, not moving any area of the body.
Increase the challenge by slightly bending the elbows, and then finally going to a straight arm position.
Push with one arm and pull with the other, flexing the stick, and hold for 1-2 seconds before switching the role of the arms.
Complete the designated number of reps before switching sides.

name: Lead off shuffle to steal
cues: Start in your base stealing position, push off of your imaginary base shuffle to see the imaginary play and then cross over to sprint as if you were stealing a base.

name: Low Back Release Stick Mobility
cues: Position yourself in a 1/2 kneeling position with the stick positioned at the lower back with palms facing forward.
You can work straight on or at an angle, focusing more on the right or left side.
Work the stick up and down the back looking for the most sensitive areas to release.

name: lower body disassociation stick mobility
cues: In a golf width stance, position 1 stick vertically in front of the body, pressing down into the ground with both hands.
While trying not to move the chest, rotate the pelvis/hips from one side to the other under control.
Keep the hands in line with the chest and pressing down to create core stability.

name: Lower Leg Release Stick Mobility
cues: Position yourself in a 1/2 kneeling position and begin working the stick up and down the tissue of the outer lower leg, looking for sensitive areas.
Then work to the back side of the lower leg, spending more time in areas that are more sensitive.
Work from the top to the bottom, medial to lateral.
Work on one leg for as long as needed before switching legs.

name: March with side bend over front knee
cues: Raise front knee to hip height and reach arms to the same side as the raised knee, stay tall and allow the spine to bend to the side, this requires focus and balance.

name: Mid Back Release Stick Mobility
cues: Position yourself in a 1/2 kneeling position with the stick positioned between the crux of the elbows and the mid-back.
Roll the stick up and down, and across the mid back while working in small torso rotations.

name: Post Tibialis Release
cues:
Technique: Posterior Tibialis Release 
Purpose: 
 To release tension and restore glide in the posterior tibialis, a deep stabilizing muscle of the lower leg that plays a critical role in: 
 
Foot arch support 
Ankle inversion 
Deceleration during gait 
Controlling pronation 
 
Releasing this muscle can reduce overuse tension, relieve medial shin or ankle discomfort, and improve overall foot-ankle mechanics — especially in runners, lifters, and those with flat feet or posterior tibial tendinopathy.

Target Area: 
 
Posterior tibialis muscle, located deep behind the medial edge of the tibia (shin bone), wrapping behind the medial malleolus (inner ankle bone) and inserting along the foot arch.

Setup: 
 
You’ll need a massage ball, lacrosse ball, or thumb/pinpoint pressure (can be therapist-assisted or self-performed).
Optional: foam roller or massage gun if working more globally.

Movement Pattern: Self-Release (Seated or Sidelying Position) 
 
Locate the Area: 
 
 
Sit with your ankle crossed over your opposite knee (figure-4 position), or lie on your side.
Find the posterior-medial aspect of your tibia — just behind the shin bone.
Palpate the area by pressing your fingers or ball along the inside border of your lower leg, especially 2–6 inches above the ankle.

Apply Pressure: 
 
 
Use your thumb, fingers, or massage ball to press gently into the muscle belly, not the bone.
Hold static pressure on any tender or tight spots for 20–30 seconds, or apply slow stripping strokes along the muscle fibers (from mid-calf toward the ankle).

Mobilize (Optional): 
 
 
While maintaining pressure, move your foot through dorsiflexion and plantarflexion, or inversion/eversion.

name: Prone diaphragmatic breathing over ball explained

cues: Begin lying face down, so that your stomach is on the floor.

Then slowly return to starting position.

name: Prone Shoulder Extension - Hover
cues: Lie on your chest with your working arm straight to your side with your non-working arm supporting your forehead with your forearm.
The working arm can be internally rotated, making a fist with the thumb up or with the palm open facing up.
Position an object directing outside of the working arm that you can hover over without compensation, but is still high enough to challenge you.
Take a breath in to create tension, then work to maximally extend the shoulder as high into the air as you can.
Keeping the elbow straight throughout, slowly hover over the object then slowly set the arm down on the other side.
Reset your tension, then slowly bring the arm back up and over the object, and return to the start position.
Complete for the designated number of reps before switching sides.
You can also position multiple objects outside of the working arm, causing you to perform multiple hover challenges with each rep.

name: Prone Shoulder Extension ERR
cues: Lie on your chest with your working arm straight to your side with your non-working arm supporting your forehead with your forearm.
The working arm can be internally rotated, making a fist with the thumb up or with the palm open facing up.
Take a breath in to create tension, then work to maximally extend the shoulder as high into the air as you can.
Keeping the elbow straight throughout, begin to draw either large or small clockwise circles with the working arm.
Complete the designated number of rotations, then switch directions and draw counter-clockwise circles.
Slowly bring the arm back to the ground before switching arms and completing the same process on the other side.

name: Prone Shoulder Flexion Abduction PRLO
cues: Lie on your chest with your working arm in a flexed/abducted position with your non-working arm supporting your forehead with your forearm.
Depending on your active range of shoulder flexion, you may have your hand on the floor or elevated onto a yoga block in various positions.
You can perform this with a closed fist or open palm.
Take a breath in and create full body tension, then work to lift the straight arm as high into the air as possible without compensation from anywhere in the body.
Hold for the prescribed amount of time, then slowly return the hand to the starting position.
Reset your tension then complete the designated number of repetitions before repeating this process on the other side.

name: Prone Shoulder Flexion ERR
cues: Lie on your chest with your working arm in a flexion position with your non-working arm supporting your forehead with your forearm.
You can perform this with a closed fist or open palm.
Take a breath in and create full body tension, then work to lift the straight arm as high into the air as possible without compensation from anywhere in the body.
Maintaining this tension, begin to draw either small or large clockwise reps with the straight arm, working to lift as high into your active end range as possible with each rep.
Complete the designated number of reps, then switch directions, slowly drawing small or large counter-clockwise circles with the working arm.
Complete the designated number of reps in this direction, then slowly return the hand to the starting position.
Switch arms, reset your tension, then complete the prescribed number of reps on the other side.

name: Prone Shoulder Flexion PRLO
cues: Lie on your chest with your working arm in a flexion position with your non-working arm supporting your forehead with your forearm.
Depending on your active range of shoulder flexion, you may have your hand on the floor or elevated onto a yoga block in various positions.
You can perform this with a closed fist or open palm.
Take a breath in and create full body tension, then work to lift the straight arm as high into the air as possible without compensation from anywhere in the body.
Hold for the prescribed amount of time, then slowly return the hand to the starting position.
Reset your tension then complete the designated number of repetitions before repeating this process on the other side.

name: Propeller
cues: Grab a stick in 1 hand with the thumb up and stick vertical.
Rotate the stick side to side as far as you can under control, keeping all of the fingers on the stick the whole time.
You can alter where you feel this motion by moving your hand up or down on the stick.

cues: Holding a ring in each hand with your hands in a neutral grip and right on the rib cage, squeeze your shoulder blades together and drive your elbows back.
Position your body with your chest facing the floor with heels pressed into a stable surface or in a split stance with one foot out in front for support.
Position your body more horizontally to increase the challenge or more vertically to decrease the challenge.
Passive Stretch - for 2+ minutes, focus on breathing while you keep your body straight and allow your scapula to passively retract backwards, keeping your hands and elbows tight to the body.

PAILs - take a breath in and create full body tension, then work to protract the scapula around the rib cage at 100% for the first 10 seconds, then holding a max contraction for another 10 seconds while keeping the hands close and elbows up.
RAILs - quickly switch directions and work to retract the scapula further into retraction, drawing them closer to the midline at 100% for 15 seconds.
Relax into the new stretch position for 30 seconds and up to 2 minutes then repeat for 1-2 more reps.

name: Scapular Retraction PRLO on Wall
cues: Stand facing a wall with your working arm straight out from the shoulder with your elbow straight and fist on the wall.
Maintaining a straight elbow, shift your body forward and find your passive end range of scapula retraction.
Come out of this position slightly so that you have space to actively retract into.
Take a breath in and create full body tension, then work to maximally retract your scapula to pull your fist away from the wall.
Hold for the designated period of time then relax, and bring your fist back to the wall.
Reset your body tension and complete the designated number of reps.
Relax, switch arms, and repeat this process on the other side.
You can also perform these from multiple arm angles moving up/down and in/out.

name: Seated Ankle Eversion PAILs and RAILs
cues: While seated with one leg out, knee bent, and heel on the ground, reach across the body and grab the outside of the foot with the opposite side hand, pulling the ankle into eversion.
Use the other hand to hold the knee to make sure all the motion comes from the ankle.
Passive Stretch - hold this eversion stretch for 2+ minutes, working to fully relax into your greatest, safest range.

PAILs - take a breath in to create full body tension, then the ankle works to rotate out of the eversion position into the resistance of the hand, building up the contraction to 100% over the first 10 seconds, then holding a max contraction for another 10 seconds.
RAILs - quickly switch directions and actively rotate into more eversion at 100% for 15 seconds.
Relax into the new stretch position for 30 seconds up to 2 minutes, then repeat this same process again for 1-2 more reps before switching ankles.

name: Seated Ankle Inversion PAILs and RAILs
cues: Seated on the floor with one leg in front, achieve a passive stretch of ankle inversion by grabbing the foot from both sides and rotating the sole of the foot up.
Passive Stretch - hold this passive stretch for 2+ minutes, working to relax into the greatest possible ankle inversion stretch.
PAILs - take a breath in and create full body tension, then slowly begin working to rotate out of the position, contracting into the barrier that is the hands.
Build up the contraction over the first 10 seconds, working up to 100% contraction.
Hold the 100% PAILs contraction for another 10 seconds.
RAILs - quickly switch directions and actively rotate the ankle into more inversion, holding a max effort contraction for 15 seconds.
Relax into the new stretch position and hold the passive stretch for 30 seconds to 2 minutes and repeat for 1-2 more reps before repeating the process on the other side.

name: Seated Ankle Inversion PAILs and RAILs Alt Setup
cues: While seated with one leg out, knee bent, and heel on the ground, grab the outside of the foot with the opposite side hand, pulling the ankle into inversion.
Use the other hand to grab the top of the knee, holding it in place with by creating a medial to lateral tension.
Passive Stretch - hold this inversion stretch for 2+ minutes, working to relax into your greatest, safest range.

PAILs - take a breath in to create full body tension, then the ankle works to rotate out of the inversion position into the resistance of the hand, building up the contraction to 100% over the first 10 seconds, then holding a max contraction for another 10 seconds.
RAILs - quickly switch directions and actively rotate into more inversion at 100% for 15 seconds.
Relax into the new stretch position for 30 seconds up to 2 minutes, then repeat this same process again for 1-2 more rounds before switching ankles.

name: Shinbox Vertical Stick Torso Rotation
cues: Position yourself in a shinbox position with one knee forward and one knee facing to the side.
The stick will be placed vertically into the ground in line with the midline of the thigh.
The hand that is on the same side of the forward leg will be vertical grabbing the top of the stick while the opposite hand will reach across and grab the stick right above the lower handle.
Push the stick into the ground and create an active torso rotation, moving right to left 5 times.
Expand the range of motion with each rep before locking in the 5th rep and holding for 5 seconds on each side.

name: Shoulder Abduction Eccentric Neural Grooving On Wall
cues: Position yourself with a wall, doorway, or stable upright to the side of the arm that you are planning to train.
Position your elbow on the upright approximately straight out from the shoulder, although it can be slightly above or below depending on your training needs.
In a split stance with your opposite foot forward and your elbow bent to 90 degrees, rotate your body towards the upright approximately 30-45 degrees so that you are facing it.
Take a breath in and create a full body contraction and begin pressing your elbow/arm into the upright, creating a contraction on the pec and inside shoulder of the working side.
Maintaining this contraction, slowly begin to rotate your body away from the upright so that you finish with your chest forward and elbow out to the side of your body.
Relax, bring yourself back to the starting position, reset your tension, and complete the designated number of reps.
The amount of reps, the time for each rep, and the amount of tension you create will be variables dependent on your program.

cues: Position your body in a kneeling position laying over the top of a stability ball, using your non-working arm to wrap around the ball for support.
Taking the working arm into a zone of flexion with the elbow straight, grasping a stick that is vertical with the base pressing into the floor.
Slowly walk your hand up the dowel, finding your passive end range of shoulder flexion in that zone.

Take a deep breath in and create full body tension squeezing the ball tight, and slowly loosen the grip on the dowel trying to maintain an active contraction as close to your passive end range as possible.
Hold for the designated period of time, then reset your grip on the dowel.
Walk your hand up the dowel if possible, then reset your tension and perform the next repetition.
Perform the prescribed number of repetitions then repeat this process on the other side.

name: Shoulder Flexion PRLO on Ball w Stick
cues: Position your body in a kneeling position laying over the top of a stability ball, using your non-working arm to wrap around the ball for support.
Taking the working arm into a zone of flexion with the elbow straight, grasping a stick that is vertical with the base pressing into the floor.
Slowly walk your hand up the dowel, finding your passive end range of shoulder flexion in that zone.
Walk your hand back down a couple inches or about 10-15 degrees so that you have space to actively contract into.
Take a deep breath in and create full body tension squeezing the ball tight, and work to contract into shoulder flexion, lifting the base of the dowel off of the floor.
Hold for the designated period of time, then slowly return the dowel to the floor.
If you were able to easily clear the floor without compensation, walk your hand up the dowel slightly, then reset your tension and perform the next repetition.
Perform the prescribed number of repetitions then repeat this process on the other side.

name: Side Lying Hip Adduction - Hover
cues: Position yourself in a side lying position with your working leg side on the ground with your leg straight, and top leg bent with your foot flat on the ground in front of your body.

Depending on your mobility, you may lay all the way down on your side, position yourself with your elbow on the floor, or support a more upright torso with your arm outstretched and hand on the floor - the more upright your torso, the more challenging this will be.
Position a small object like a tennis ball or yoga block either in front or behind the target leg's ankle.
Take a breath in and create a full body contraction, then work to lift your straight leg as high into the air as possible, making sure not to move any other part of the body or bend the working leg.
Slowly hover over the object, then slowly lower your leg back down to the floor on the other side.

name: Side Lying Hip Adduction PRLO Knee Hinge
cues: Position yourself in a side lying position with your working leg side on the ground with your leg straight, and top leg bent with your foot flat on the ground in front of your body.

Depending on your mobility, you may lay all the way down on your side, position yourself with your elbow on the floor, or support a more upright torso with your arm outstretched and hand on the floor - the more upright your torso, the more challenging this will be.
Take a breath in and create a full body contraction, then work to lift your straight leg as high into the air as possible, making sure not to move any other part of the body or bend the working leg.
Holding the leg in the air, slowly flex the knee as far as possible while keeping the upper leg in line with the body, then fully extend the knee until it is locked out.
Repeat this process until you have completed the designated number of reps.
Slowly lower the leg back down to the floor.
Switch sides and repeat this process on the other leg, always working to keep the leg as high as possible while performing the knee hinges.

name: Side Lying Hip Internal Rotation PRLO
cues: Position yourself in a side-lying position with your legs stacked and knees and hips bent to 90 degrees.
Squeeze an object between your knees with your top leg's ankle on top of a stool, bench, or box at or very near your active end range of hip internal rotation.
Take a breath in and create full-body tension and work to lift the top foot/ankle off of the surface while maintaining the squeeze on the object between the knees.
Hold for the designated period of time before slowly setting the foot/ankle back down.
Reset your tension, then complete the designated number of reps.
Relax, switch sides, then repeat this process on the other leg for the designated number of reps.

name: Side Lying Open books
cues: Start in a side lying position with neck support on foam roll, yoga block, or pillow.
Bring hips and knees up to a 90/90 position as if sitting on a chair.
Grab top knee with bottom arm to maintain pelvis position.
With the top hand grasp the ribs closest to the floor and begin to open the top shoulder towards the floor.
Lead the motion with the top shoulder blade.
Attempt to get deeper rotation with each repetition.
Remember to breath out while rotating to relax lung tissue.
Repeat on opposite side for prescribed number of sets and repetitions.

name: Side-Lying Shoulder Internal Rotation PRH
cues: With the hips flexed, lie on the side of the arm that you are aiming to train, with your head supported and the shoulder on the floor.

Hold for the designated period of time, then take the support hand back to the bottom arm and relax back into your passive range.
Reset your tension then complete the designated number of reps.
You can also train from multiple angles of internal rotation by positioning your elbow slightly above or below straight out from the shoulder.
Relax, switch sides, then repeat this process on the other arm.

name: Side-Lying Shoulder Internal Rotation PRLO
cues: With the hips flexed, lie on the side of the arm that you are aiming to train, with your head supported and the shoulder on the floor.
Your arm will be straight out in front slightly below horizontal with the elbow bent to 90 degrees.

Focus on breathing while relaxing and keeping the shoulder pinned to the floor, using the top hand to guide the bottom arm into more internal rotation, finding your passive end range by making sure to push at the wrist.
Then come out of this position slightly so that you have space to actively contract into.
Take a breath in and create full body tension, then work to create a maximal internal rotation contraction pulling the working arm away from the support arm.
Hold for the designated period of time, then relax and bring working arm back to the support arm.
Reset your tension then complete the designated number of reps.
You can also train from multiple angles of internal rotation by positioning your elbow slightly above or below straight out from the shoulder.
Relax, switch sides, then repeat this process on the other arm.

Spinal Wave
cues: Begin by kneeling on an exercise mat or floor, positioning your knees and feet hip-width apart, with your feet dorsiflexed toes pointing towards your body.
Slowly lean forward to place your hands on the mat, positioning them directly under your shoulders at shoulder-width with your fingers facing forward.
Reposition your hands and knees as necessary so that your knees are directly under your hips and hands are directly under your shoulders.
Breathe.
Begin to arch your back one vertebra or segment at a time starting from your pelvis and working all the way up to the neck in a wave like motion.
Hold that position and start flexing from the pelvis and working all the way back up to the neck one segement at a time in the reverse wave pattern.
Maximizing movement throughout the back and between vertebrae relies on the ability to let go of or preventing unnecessary tension.
Use a relaxed pace of breath to calm both the mind and body as you execute this exercise.
Repeat for prescribe number of repetitions.

name: Standing Ankle Dorsiflexion - gastroc focus - full
cues: Stand facing a wall with a split stance, have your working leg back and non-working leg forwards.
Passive Stretch - achieve a passive stretch on the upper calf by locking out your knee while keeping your heel on the floor, working to close down the angle of the ankle.
Hold this position for 2+ minutes working to relax into a progressively deeper stretch position.

PAILs - take a breath in to create full body tension, then slowly begin pressing the bottom of the foot into the floor as if you were pressing down on a gas pedal, ramping up the contraction to 100% over the first 10 seconds, then holding the max contraction for another 10 seconds.
RAILs - quickly switch directions, working to lift the bottom of the foot off of the floor, pulling yourself deeper into the stretch at 100% contraction for 15 seconds.
Relax into the new stretch position for 30 seconds up to 2 minutes, and repeat for 1-2 more reps before switching ankles.

name: Standing Ankle Dorsiflexion PAILs-RAILs - Soleus Focus
cues: Stand facing a wall with a split stance, have your working leg back and non-working leg forwards.

Passive Stretch - achieve a passive stretch on the soleus (lower calf) by bending your knee and shifting your hips back while keeping your heel on the floor, working to close down the angle of the ankle.
Hold this position for 2+ minutes working to relax into a progressively deeper stretch position.

PAILs - take a breath in to create full body tension, then slowly begin pressing the bottom of the foot into the floor as if you were pressing down on a gas pedal, ramping up the contraction to 100% over the first 10 seconds, then holding the max contraction for another 10 seconds.
RAILs - quickly switch directions, working to lift the bottom of the foot off of the floor, pulling yourself deeper into the stretch at 100% contraction for 15 seconds.
Relax into the new stretch position for 30 seconds up to 2 minutes, and repeat for 1-2 more reps before switching ankles.

name: Standing Ankle Eversion w KB PAILs and RAILs
cues: Lie a kettlebell between your feet on its side with the handle facing away from the ankle that you are aiming to train.
Passive Stretch - while holding sticks or the wall for stability, position the inside of your foot on the floor with the outside of your foot on the handle of the kettlebell.
Position your body over the kettlebell and step your non-working leg behind the working leg, pulling yourself deeper into a passive stretch of ankle eversion and hold the stretch for 2+ minutes.
PAILs - take a breath in to create full body tension, then begin slowly pressing the outside of the foot onto the handle of the kettlebell, contracting the muscles that are being stretched.
Build the contraction up to 100% over the first 10 seconds, then hold the max contraction for another 10 seconds.

RAILs - quickly switch directions, working to pull outside of the foot off of the handle of the kettlebell while shifting your hips towards the working leg, pulling yourself deeper into an ankle eversion stretch and hold the max contraction for 15 seconds.
Relax into the new stretch position for 30 seconds up to 2 minutes and repeat the process again for 1-2 more reps before switching legs.

name: Standing Ankle Eversion w/ Slant Board
cues: Standing over a slant board using dowels or a wall for stability, position the inside edge of your foot along the bottom edge of the board, and step the non-working leg behind the working leg.
Passive Stretch - achieve a passive stretch of ankle eversion by shifting the hips toward from the working leg, focusing on relaxing deeper into the stretch for 2+ minutes.

PAILs - take a breath in and create full body tension, then begin pressing the outer edge of the foot onto the slant board, ramping up the contracting to 100% over the first 10 seconds, then hold the max contraction for another 10 seconds.

RAILs - quickly switch directions, working to lift the outside edge of the foot off of the board while simultaneously shifting the hips in the direction of the working ankle, holding the max contraction for 15 seconds.
Relax into the new stretch position for 30 seconds and up to 2 minutes, then repeat for 1-2 more reps before switching ankles.

name: Standing Ankle Inversion w/ Slant Board - abbr.
cues: Standing over a slant board using dowels or a wall for stability, position the outside edge of your foot along the bottom edge of the board, and step away from the working leg.
Passive Stretch - achieve a passive stretch of ankle inversion by shifting the hips away from the working leg, focusing on relaxing deeper into the stretch for 2+ minutes.

PAILs - take a breath in and create full body tension, then begin pressing the instep of the foot onto the slant board, ramping up the contracting to 100% over the first 10 seconds, then hold the max contraction for another 10 seconds.
RAILs - quickly switch directions, working to lift the instep off of the board while simultaneously shifting the hips away from the working ankle, holding the max contraction for 15 seconds.
Relax into the new stretch position for 30 seconds and up to 2 minutes, then repeat for 1-2 more reps before switching ankles.

name: Standing Ankle Inversion with KB
cues: Lie a kettlebell between your feet on its side with the handle facing the direction of the ankle that you are aiming to train.
Passive Stretch - position the outside of your foot on the floor with your instep on the handle of the kettlebell.
Position your body over the kettlebell and shift your hips away from the working leg, pulling yourself deeper into a passive stretch of ankle inversion and hold the stretch for 2+ minutes.
PAILs - take a breath in a create full body tension, then begin slowly pressing the instep of the foot onto the handle of the kettlebell, contracting the muscles that are being stretched.
Build the contraction up to 100% over the first 10 seconds, then hold the max contraction for another 10 seconds.

RAILs - quickly switch directions, working to pull your instep off of the handle of the kettlebell while shifting your hips, pulling yourself deeper into an ankle inversion stretch and hold the max contraction for 15 seconds.
Relax into the new stretch position for 30 seconds up to 2 minutes and repeat the process again for 1-2 more reps before switching legs.

name: Standing Bicep Curl on Cable Machine
Standing Cable Tricep Extension with V-Bar
Standing Hip Abduction With a Band

cues: Stand on one leg with a box, bench, or another sturdy object in front of you with a height that is just below your active end range.

You can hold two sticks in front of you with outstretched arms and drive them down into the ground, or you can position yourself with your back to a wall to aid in balance and make sure you stand straight up throughout the set.
Position your target leg foot on top of the box.
Take a breath in and create full-body tension, driving the sticks into the floor or hands into the wall behind you.
Moving only the target leg, work to lift the knee as high into your active end range as possible, lifting your foot off of the box.
Hold for the designated period of time, then slowly set your foot back onto the box.
Reset your tension, and complete for the designated number of reps.
Switch legs and repeat the process on the other side.

name: Standing Hip Flexion Hovers
cues: Stand on one leg with a box, bench, or another sturdy object in front of you with a height that is just below your active end range.

You can hold two sticks in front of you with outstretched arms and drive them down into the ground, or you can position yourself with your back to a wall to aid in balance and make sure you stand straight up throughout the set.
Position your target leg foot on top of the box with a small obstacle either outside or inside the foot.
Take a breath in and create full-body tension, driving the sticks into the floor or hands into the wall behind you.
Moving only the target leg, work to lift the knee as high into your active end range as possible, lifting your foot off of the box and over the obstacle.
Hover over the obstacle, then slowly set your foot back onto the box on the other side.
Reset your tension, then lift up and back over to the start position.
Complete this process for the designated number of reps.
Switch legs and repeat the process on the other side.
You can also set up multiple objects either inside or outside of the foot, forcing you to complete multiple hover challenges on each set.

name: Standing Hip Flexors With a Band
Standing Rope Bicep Curl on Cable Machine
Standing Scapula End Range Rotations w KB
Standing Scapula ERR w DB/KB
cues: In standing position, hold a kettlebell, dumbbell, or any weighted object in your working hand directly at your side with a straight elbow.
This weight should challenge you but allow you to perform the movement without compensation.
Take a breath in and create full body tension, then slow elevate your scapula, pulling your shoulder to your ear.
In a circular pattern, find your maximal scapula elevation then retract your shoulder blade, pulling it towards the spine under control.
Maintaining this circular pattern, find your end range of retraction while your depress your scapula, pulling it back and down.
Find your end range of scapula depression, then work right into scapula protraction, pushing the shoulder forwards.
Slowly complete the designated number of reps in this direction before changing directions and completing the designated number of reps in the opposite direction.
Switch arms and repeat this process on the other side.
Make sure to use slow, controlled circular motions while maintaining body tension and a straight elbow.

name: Standing serratus breathing against wall explained
Standing Shoulder Abduction PRH on Wall
cues: In a standing position with a wall to your side, position your working arm out to your side with elbow bent to approximately 90 degrees and elbow, forearm, and hand on the wall.
Focus on your breathing while you shift your body forward and towards the wall, increasing the stretch of shoulder abduction.
Take a breath in and create full body tension, then work to pull the working arm away from the wall and further into shoulder abduction.
Slightly shift your body away from the wall, working to maintain this maximal contraction for the designated period of time.
Shift your body back to the wall, find the passive stretch, reset your tension, then complete for the designated number of reps.
Relax, switch sides, then repeat this process on the other arm.

name: Standing Single Arm Cable Bicep Curl
Standing Single Leg Dumbbell Calf Raise
Step Back with Opposite Shoulder Flexion
Stick dead bug iso hold
cues: Lie on your back with your back flat to the floor and both legs straight.
Flex one hip to 90 degrees with the knee also bent to 90 degrees and both ankles flexed.
Holding the stick in the hand on the opposite side of the bent knee, drive the base of the stick into the top of the bent knee.
Extend the free arm overhead as high as you can while maintaining your back flat to the floor and hold for the designated time before switching sides.
You can increase the challenge by placing your hand higher up on the stick.

name: Stick Hip Hinge Spine Flexion Extension
cues: Position the stick vertically in front of the body driving the base of the stick into the ground with both hands.
Get into a deep hinge position, getting as long as possible through the spine with straight arms.
Keeping tension into the stick, flex the spine working to create a large curve, driving the spine to the sky.
Then change directions, working into extension, driving your sternum towards the floor.
Complete 5-6 controlled reps in each direction.

name: Stick Mobility Foot release
cues: Position the stick on the ground in front of the body.
Slowly and deliberately roll around the foot, looking for sensitive areas.
Work the medial and lateral portions of the foot, taking more time in the troubled areas.
Spend as much time as needed on one foot before switching sides.

name: Stick stork turns
cues: The stork turns help to isolate the lower body rotation from a fixed upper body and helps promote closed chain hip rotation.
Place your golf club in front of you, planted on the floor with both hands grasping the top of the handle.
Lift one leg up into a “stork” position.
Next, using the lifted leg as a point of reference, rotate the lower body, bringing the knee across midline back and forward while keeping the upper torso still.
Perform 3-5 reps.

name: Stick Taps
cues: Standing on one leg, lift the other leg, bending the hip and knee to 90 degrees.
Position the stick vertically right outside of the up leg and drive the stick down into the ground with the same side arm.
Keeping the hip at 90 degrees, perform stick taps, internally rotating the elevated leg and tapping the stick with the outside of the foot.
Complete 5-6 reps on the first leg before switching legs and repeating this process on the other side.

name: Stork Turns
cues: Stand on one leg and position the stick vertically slightly in front and to the outside of the standing leg, with the same side arm driving the stick down into the ground.
Bend the other knee and position the top of the foot directly behind the back of the knee of the standing leg.
Work to rotate the pelvis side to side while limiting motion throughout the rest of the body.
Complete 5-6 reps in both directions on one leg before switching legs and repeating this process on the other leg.

name: Superband Anterior Shoulder Stretch Contract Relax
Superband Lat Stretch
cues: Attach flexvit or resistance band about shoulder height.
Wrap hand through the opposite end and start to hinge hips back keeping arms straight and back flat (avoid rounding back) allowing your chest to drop to the floor.
Breath deep to expand the rib cage then allow the chest to drop further to the floor.
Should feel a stretch down the outside of the shoulder to the low back.
Should not be feeling any shoulder or low back pain with this.
Back off the stretch by walking feet closer to anchor if feeling any pain.

name: Superband Posterior Shoulder Stretch
cues:
Superband Posterior Shoulder Stretch. 
 
 
This can be done dynamically as shown or you can hold passively and then perform PAILs RAILs contractions for optimal neurological adaptation. Watch our "PAILs and RAILs explained" video for instructions.
Put your hand through the band and then grab both straps of the band.
Walk laterally away from the origin of the band until you feel a substantial stretch on the back of your shoulder and mid-back.

Rotate in and out of the stretch for dynamic stretch. Or hold a passive stretch and then perform PAILs and RAILs contractions for maximal neurological adaptation. 
 
 
 
Repeat on the other side.

name: Supinated Chin Over Vertical Plane Hold
Supine Figure 4 Hip External Rotation PAILs-RAILs
cues: Lie on your back with your non-working leg bent to roughly 90 degrees and foot flat on the floor.
Take your working leg across the body and position the outside of your ankle on the thigh of the non-working leg, then lift the non-working leg off of the ground.
Depending on your mobility, you can hold across the shin, back of the thigh, or on top of the knee of the non-working leg.
Passive Stretch - for 2+ minutes work on breathing and relaxing into a progressively deeper stretch on the outside of the hip.

PAILs - take a breath in and create full body tension, then slowly begin rotating the outside of the working leg into the thigh of the non-working leg, building up to 100% over the first 10 seconds, then holding a max contraction for another 10 seconds.
RAILs - quickly switch directions, working to rotate the leg off of the non-working leg thigh at 100% for 15 seconds.
Relax deeper into the stretch for another 30 seconds, and up to 2 minutes.
Repeat for 1-2 more reps on that leg before switching sides.

name: Supine Hip Flexion PRLO
cues: Position yourself on your back with one leg straight and pull the other knee as high up to the chest as possible into your passive end range of hip flexion.
Come out of that position slightly by lowering the knee so you can contract into your active end range.
Take a breath in and create full body tension, driving as much tension into the hip flexors as possible.
Moving only the target leg, work to lift the knee as high into your active end range as possible, pulling your leg away from the support of the hands.
Hold for the designated period of time, then slowly lower your leg back down to your hands.
Reset your tension, and complete for the designated number of reps.
Switch legs and repeat the process on the other side.
You can also train in the full zone of hip flexion, meaning you can train with the knee up and out to the side, and all of the zones in between.

name: Supine Knees Bent Posterior Pelvic Tilt
Supine stick shoulder raise to pulldown to press
cues: Start in a supine position with knees bent and feet flat with the stick across the waist with a double overhand grip.
Work to keep the lower back flat to the floor throughout the movement.
Grab the stick wider than shoulder width and work to actively pull the hands apart.
Perform an active shoulder raise, taking the stick overhead as far as you can while keeping the back flat to the floor.
From the overhead position, perform an active pulldown while working to pull the hands apart.
From there, press the arms/stick overhead while driving the hands in.
After the press, take the stick back down to waist height while pushing the stick in with straight arms.
Remember: active pull apart of the stick while you press and pulldown, active press into the stick while you press up and return to the start position.
You could perform the whole sequence as one rep, or stay in the overhead position and perform push/pulls for reps.

name: T-spine rotations with stability ball adduction
cues: Stand over a stability ball, squeezing the ball between the legs with a stick positioned horizontally across the chest with the arms crossed.
Create a shoulder turn in both directions while not letting the hips turn.
Perform the designated number of reps in each direction, working the squeeze the ball harder and rotate a bit further each time.

Tissue Exploration - Front Of Shoulder
cues: To improve external rotation we will focus on releasing the internal rotators.
These muscles are mostly located on the front side of the shoulder.
Begin laying on the involved side with the foam roller on the outer aspect of your shoulder blade beneath the armpit.
Use your legs to help propel your body up and down on the roller.
Seek out tender areas and oscillate over the region for no longer than 90 seconds aiming for reducing the level of tenderness.
Utilize breath, rib position, and arm position to increase or decrease muscular and fascial tension as you release the tender areas.
Roll onto the front side of the shoulder next and seek out other tender areas.
Caution over bony prominences or placing pressure over areas that cause throbbing or numbness sensation.

name: Tissue Exploration - Lats
cues: To improve external rotation we will focus on releasing the internal rotators.
The latissimus dorsi is a large internal rotator that attaches from our shoulder down to our low back and pelvis.
Begin laying on the involved side with the foam roller on the outer and back side of your shoulder blade.
Use your legs to help propel your body up and down on the roller.
Seek out tender areas and oscillate over the region for no longer than 90 seconds aiming for reducing the level of tenderness.
Utilize breath, rib position, and arm position to increase or decrease muscular and fascial tension as you release the tender areas.
Explore the whole length of the muscle from the shoulder down to the pelvis.
Caution over bony prominences or placing pressure over areas that cause throbbing or numbness sensation.

name: Tissue Exploration - Spine
cues: To mobilize the tissues of the spine you can use a foam roller or a wedge.
You can utilize the wedge on specific points of your mid and upper back to influence extension.
Lay on your back with your knees bent and feet flat. allow the bony aspect of your spine to sit in the middle of the wedge and relax over the top.
If using the foam roller lay perpendicular with knees bent and feet flat.
You can support your head with your hands and begin rolling up and down on the foam roll in your mid and upper back.
You can influence pressure on either side of the spine by shifting body weight.
You can also extend over the top of the roller to influence more extension.
To get into the deeper QL muscles rotate trunk on roller about 30-45 degrees and try to roll the area between the lower ribs and pelvis.
Take caution rolling over bony prominences.

name: Tissue Exploration Adductors Front and Inner Thigh
cues: Place foam roller on floor and begin by rolling on the lateral/anterior aspect of the hip.

Use hands/elbows and off leg to support your weight so that you are only placing about 50% of your body weight on the foam roller.  roll up and down/side to side scouring for tender points along the front of the hip and inner thigh and oscillate over those tender points up to 90 seconds, aiming for reducing the level of tenderness.
Once tenderness reduces, find 2-3 more tender points to work on.
Caution of going over bony prominences or placing pressure over anything that causes nervy or throbbing sensations.

name: Tissue Exploration Back Of Thigh
cues: Place foam roller on the floor and sit on foam roller, lean to one side to place pressure on theback of the thigh/hamstrings.

Place about 50% of your full weight onto the foam roller using hands and other leg to support yourself. roll up and down/side to side scouring for tender points along the back of the hip and thigh and oscillate over those tender points up to 90 seconds, aiming for reducing the level of tenderness.
You may alter positioning of leg and hip (crossing leg or keeping straight) to fully explore where the tendern points are.
Once tenderness reduces, find 2-3 more tender points to work on.
Caution of going over bony prominences or placing pressure over anything that causes nervy or throbbing sensations.

name: Tissue Exploration Feet
cues: Using a lacross ball, golf ball or something of similar size, place ball on the floor and place foot over the ball with moderate pressure.
Scour for tender points by rolling up/down and side to side.
Once tender points are found, oscillate over these points until tenderness reduces for a maximum of 90 seconds.
Avoid areas that produce sharp pains or nerve symptoms.

name: Tissue Exploration Lower Leg
cues: Using a massage gun, foam roll, or massage ball, apply moderate pressure to the calf and scour for tender points throughout the region.
Once tender points are found, oscillate over these points until tenderness reduces for a maximum of 90 seconds.
Avoid areas that produce sharp pains or nerve symptoms.

name: Tissue Exploration Posterior Hip
cues: Place foam roller on the floor and sit on foam roller, leaning to one side to place pressure on the glute that needs to be worked on.

Place about 50% of your full weight onto the foam roller using hands and other leg to support yourself. roll up and down/side to side scouring for tender points along the back of the hip and thigh and oscillate over those tender points up to 90 seconds, aiming for reducing the level of tenderness.

Once tenderness reduces, find 2-3 more tender points to work on.
Caution of going over bony prominences or placing pressure over anything that causes nervy or throbbing sensations.

Use your legs to help propel your body up and down on the roller.

cues: Position yourself in a quadruped base position with either both hands or one hand down on the floor directly under your shoulders with your elbows straight.
Shift your hips back slightly to give yourself active range of wrist extension to move into.
Take a breath in and create full body tension, then begin pressing your palms into the floor by contracting your wrists into flexion.
Maintaining this flexion contraction, slowly begin shifting your hips and body forward creating a stretch in the forearms while they contract.
Shift forward until you find your active end range of wrist extension, then relax and bring yourself back to the starting position.
Reset your tension then complete for the designated number of reps.
The amount of reps, the time for each rep, and the amount of tension you create will be variables dependent on your program.

name: W Turns
cues: The W turn also helps with upper body rotation but focuses more on improving external shoulder rotation which is needed for the trail arm in the back-swing and the lead arm on the follow-through.
Place a club across the shoulders and behind your neck and grab both ends of the club with your hands.
Your elbows should be pointing down to the floor.
This should create a “W” position with your arms.
Next, get into the 5-iron position and rotate the upper body right and left while keeping the lower body stable.
Perform 3-5 reps.

name: Walking lunge with rotation
cues: Lunge forward with an upright torso and arms to yourside.
Then rotate over the front knee with shoulders and spine.
Legs and head should maintain their position as you rotate shoulders and spine.

name: Wide Stance Lateral Hip Shift Torso Rotation
cues: Position yourself in a wide stance with the stick placed horizontally across the lower back with your hands at each end of the stick.
Shift your weight into 1 hip while rotating your torso in the same direction.
As you shift to one side the other leg will straighten.
Then shift your weight to the other hip while straightening the other leg and rotating the torso in the direction of the hip you are shifting to.
Make sure to keep the eyes down for the duration of the set.
Complete 5-6 controlled reps in each direction.

name: Wide Stance Single Stick Monkey Hang Hinge and Reach Level 1
cues: Position yourself in a wide stance with 1 stick vertically to the side.
Grabbing at the top of the stick, drive the base of the stick into the ground right inside the big toe.
Hinge at the hips and reach across the body at grab the middle of the stick with the other hand.
Slowly shift the hips side to side for the designated time or number of reps.

name: Wide Stance Single Stick Monkey Hang Hinge and Reach Level 2
cues: Position yourself in a wide stance with 1 stick vertically to the side.
Grabbing at the top of the stick, drive the base of the stick into the ground right inside the big toe.
Hinge at the hips and reach across the body towards the base of the stick while shifting your hips away from the stick.
Slowly shift the hips toward the stick, rotate the torso, and reach the arm away from the stick straight out to the side.
Repeat this process back and forth for the designated time or number of reps.

name: Wide Stance Single Stick Monkey Hang Hinge and Reach Level 3
cues: Position yourself in a wide stance with 1 stick vertically to the side.
Grabbing at the top of the stick, drive the base of the stick into the ground right inside the big toe.
Hinge at the hips and reach across the body and grab the base of the stick while shifting your hips away from the stick.
Actively pushing with both hands into the ground, slowly shift the hips towards the stick and away from the stick.
Repeat this process back and forth for the designated time or number of reps.
Make sure to maintain tension throughout, while focusing on shifting the weight in your hips side to side and rotating the torso to facilitate the best stretch.

name: Wrist Capsule Extension
cues: Extend one arm straight out in front with a closed fist and flexed wrist.
Take your opposite hand and grab onto the skin underneath the forearm of the working arm and pull towards your elbow.
While gently pulling the skin back towards you, extend the wrist of the working arm and slowly open up the fingers.
Come back down to wrist flexion, make a fist, reset the pull of the forearm, then repeat this process for the prescribed number of reps.
Repeat this process, holding the extended position for 1 slow breath.
Switch arms and repeat this process on the other side.

name: Wrist CAR How to
cues: Start Position: Sit or stand comfortably with your arm in front of you, keeping your elbow bent at 90 degrees or straight, depending on your comfort.
Your forearm should be steady, and you can rest it on a table or your opposite hand to help keep it stable.
Engage Your Core: Brace your core slightly to avoid compensating with other parts of your body.
Grip Your Forearm: With your opposite hand, gently grip your forearm just below the wrist to ensure that movement is isolated to the wrist and doesn’t extend into the forearm or elbow.
Move Slowly and Deliberately: Begin by slowly moving your wrist in a circle.
Move it through the full range of motion as you explore each direction — flexing forward, extending back, tilting side to side, and rotating fully.
Focus on Control: Keep the movement slow, controlled, and as smooth as possible.
Think of “drawing” the largest possible circle with your wrist while avoiding any jerking or compensatory movement.
Reverse the Direction: After a few reps in one direction, switch to the opposite direction and repeat.
Perform for Reps or Time: Complete 5-10 controlled circles in each direction or work for about 30-60 seconds per wrist.

name: Wrist Extension PRH - Open Kinetic Chain
cues: In a kneeling, seated, or standing position, position your working arm across the body with the elbow bent to approximately 90 degrees, and use the opposite hand to bend the wrist into an extended position, finding your passive end range.
Focus on your breathing while you use the control hand to guide the working wrist into an extended position by pushing on the palm of the working hand.
Take a breath in and create full body tension, then work to extend the wrist at your maximal end range.
Slowly remove the support of the control hand, working to maintain active extension as close to your passive end range as possible.
Hold for the designated period of time before relaxing and bringing the control hand back to the palm of the working hand and guiding the wrist deeper into extension.
Reset your tension then complete the designated number of reps.
Relax, switch arms, then repeat this process on the other side.

name: Wrist Extension PRLO - open chain
cues: In a kneeling, seated, or standing position, position your working arm across the body with the elbow bent to approximately 90 degrees, and use the opposite hand to bend the wrist into an extended position, finding your passive end range.
Then come out of this position slightly so that you have space to actively contract into.
Take a breath in and create full body tension, then work to extend the wrist at your maximal end range, pulling the working hand away from the control hand.
Hold for the designated period of time before relaxing and bringing the working hand back to the palm of the control hand.
Reset your tension then complete the designated number of reps.
Relax, switch arms, then repeat this process on the other side.

Focus on your breathing while you use the control hand to guide the working wrist into a flexed position by pushing on the back of the working hand.
Take a breath in and create full body tension, then work to flex the wrist at your maximal end range.
Slowly remove the support of the control hand, working to maintain active flexion as close to your passive end range as possible.
Hold for the designated period of time before relaxing and bringing the control hand back to the back of the working hand and guiding the wrist deeper into flexion.
Reset your tension then complete the designated number of reps.
Relax, switch arms, then repeat this process on the other side.

name: Wrist Flexion PRLO

cues: In a kneeling, seated, or standing position, position your working arm across the body with the elbow bent to approximately 90 degrees, and use the opposite hand to bend the wrist into a flexed position, finding your passive end range.
Then come out of this position slightly so that you have space to actively contract into.
Take a breath in and create full body tension, then work to flex the wrist at your maximal end range, pulling the working hand away from the control hand.
Hold for the designated period of time before relaxing and bringing the working hand back to the palm of the control hand.
Reset your tension then complete the designated number of reps.
Relax, switch arms, then repeat this process on the other side.

name: Wrist Flexion Stretch
cues: Extend one arm straight out in front with an open palm and extended wrist.
Take your opposite hand grab onto the skin around the forearm of the working arm and pull towards your elbow.
While gently pulling the skin towards you, flex the wrist of the working arm as far as you can, then make a fist with the hand.
Come back up to wrist extension, open the palm, reset the pull of the forearm, then repeat this process for the prescribed number of reps.
Repeat this process, holding the flexed position for 1 slow breath.
Switch arms and repeat this process on the other side.

name: wrist hinges
cues: Grab a stick in 1 hand with the thumb up and stick vertical.
Hinge at the wrist as far as you can under control alternating between pointing the stick forward and backward.
Do not let the fingers come off of the stick.
You can alter where you feel this motion by moving your hand up or down on the stick.
